chapters.name: Dawn
chapters.text: The gates are unbarred and the night's riders come in with their satchels.

chapters.name: The Wider World
chapters.text: Word from beyond our borders, as far as our eyes reach.

chapters.name: Our Works
chapters.text: What our orders have finished while we slept.

chapters.name: Our Coffers and People
chapters.text: The ledgers are read out, and the mood of the streets with them.

chapters.name: Our Cause
chapters.text: Where the house stands toward the thing it set out to do.

chapters.name: Dusk
chapters.text: The lamps are lit in the hall. The day is closed.

beats.headline: {settlement} finishes {subject}
beats.body: The masons strike their scaffolding and stand back with the crowd to look at it.

beats.headline: {settlement} musters {subject}
beats.body: New men take the oath in the square, and the drill yard is loud again by noon.

beats.headline: The treasury moves by {value}
beats.body: Taxes, farms and trade set against wages, grain and the price of keeping men under arms.

beats.headline: Unpaid men go home
beats.body: The chest is empty and the costliest company is stood down before it mutinies. Debt disbands an army as surely as any enemy.

beats.headline: Riots in {settlement}
beats.body: Order stands at {value}. Stalls are overturned, a granary is forced, and the watch is too few to be anywhere that matters.

beats.headline: {settlement} has risen in revolt
beats.body: The garrison is gone and another banner flies over the gate. What was ours this morning answers to nobody now.

beats.headline: {settlement} rises to a {subject}
beats.body: The old boundary stones are moved out and the surveyors argue cheerfully about where the new ones go.

beats.headline: {settlement} falls back to a {subject}
beats.body: What was built up is knocked down, and the town keeps only what it can still defend and feed.

beats.headline: Sickness takes hold in {settlement}
beats.body: It begins by the water and spreads by the well. The physicians burn what they can and argue about the rest.

beats.headline: {settlement} grows by {value_abs}
beats.body: More mouths, more hands, more tax. The capital is heavier today than it was yesterday.

beats.headline: {settlement} loses {value_abs} souls
beats.body: Fewer at the market and fewer on the rolls. A capital that shrinks is a house that is slipping.

beats.headline: War between {faction} and {other_faction}
beats.body: Envoys are sent home without an answer and the roads between them close. Neither side will admit to starting it.

beats.headline: {faction} and {other_faction} lay down arms
beats.body: Terms are read out in both tongues. Whether they hold is another season's business.

beats.headline: {faction} and {other_faction} are bound in alliance
beats.body: Oaths are sworn over a shared altar. Their enemies have become each other's.

beats.headline: {faction} and {other_faction} are no longer allies
beats.body: The oath is set aside without ceremony, which tells you how much it was worth.

beats.headline: {faction} and {other_faction} open their markets
beats.body: Harbour dues are agreed and the first hulls are already being loaded against it.

beats.headline: {faction} is no more
beats.body: The last of their holdings has fallen. Their name passes out of the reckoning of powers.

beats.headline: {faction} moves on {region}
beats.body: Our scouts count the dust on the road — near enough {value} men — and ride back with the number.

beats.headline: A battle is fought at {region}
beats.body: {faction} against {other_faction}. The field is decided before the light goes.

beats.headline: {settlement} is invested by {faction}
beats.body: The lines are dug and the gates are shut. Nothing goes in or out until this is settled one way or the other.

beats.headline: {settlement} runs out of grain
beats.body: The stores are down to sweepings. The garrison comes out to fight at the wall rather than starve behind it.

beats.headline: {faction} takes {settlement} from {other_faction}
beats.body: The gate is opened from the inside, whether by a ram or by an understanding. A new standard goes up before dark.

beats.headline: {subject}
beats.body: News that will be repeated all season, in every market from here to the sea.

beats.headline: Disaster strikes {settlement}
beats.body: The ground, the sea or the sky takes its turn at the place, and there is nothing to be done but count afterwards.

beats.headline: The Senate charges us: {subject}
beats.body: A charge is laid on the house, with {value} turns to answer it. The conscript fathers do not ask twice.

beats.headline: {subject}: {value} turns remain
beats.body: The charge still stands against us, and the clock on it does not stop for a quiet season.

beats.headline: The Senate is satisfied: {subject}
beats.body: The charge is discharged and the reward paid out. Someone in the curia makes a note of the house that did it.

beats.headline: The Senate is disappointed: {subject}
beats.body: The season ran out before the work did. Nothing is said aloud, which is worse than if it were.

beats.headline: {faction} is declared an enemy of the Republic
beats.body: Too loved by the people and too little trusted by the Senate. The other houses are told which side they are on.

beats.headline: We hold {value} regions
beats.body: The map is redrawn in the hall and the pins are moved to where the borders actually are.

beats.headline: The age is decided
beats.body: What was contested is settled. Whatever comes next will be somebody else's war.

beats.headline: A child is born to the house: {subject}
beats.body: The midwife is paid, the household is loud, and one more name is written into the line.

beats.headline: {subject} comes of age
beats.body: He puts on the plain toga of a man and is handed something to do with it. What he becomes is now partly our choosing.

beats.headline: {subject} marries into the house
beats.body: The contract is read, the dowry counted, and two families that were merely polite are now obliged to each other.

beats.headline: {subject} is adopted into the family
beats.body: Blood is a convenience; a useful man is a necessity. The adoption is entered on the rolls without much ceremony.

beats.headline: {subject} is named heir
beats.body: The succession is settled while it can still be settled quietly. The man passed over will remember that it was.

beats.headline: {subject} takes his place at the head of the house
beats.body: The seal changes hands in the atrium. Whatever was owed to the old man is owed to him now.

beats.headline: {subject} is dead
beats.body: The house goes into mourning and the clients gather at the door before the body is cold, to see who they should be talking to.

beats.headline: {subject} is spoken of as {detail}
beats.body: A reputation is only what enough people have decided about you. It follows him into every city he governs and every field he takes.

beats.headline: {subject} takes {detail} into his retinue
beats.body: One more useful person in the baggage train, eating our bread and earning it in a way that is hard to put on a ledger.

beats.headline: {subject} is raised up for what he did on the field
beats.body: A captain who wins a battle he had no business winning does not stay a captain. The house adopts him before somebody else does.
